The United States announced on Wednesday that it had suspended all government operations in the Mexican state of Michoacan because of a "threat to U.S. interests," including a halt to the inspections of avocados required for their export.

While the U.S. Embassy did not specify the nature of the threat in its security alert, Michoacan Gov. Alfredo Ramírez Bedolla said on social media that the temporary halt to inspections was intended to safeguard workers following recent arrests linked to extortion. The inspections are necessary for avocados to be shipped to the United States and their suspension could disrupt exports.

The western state of Michoacan is the leading exporter of avocados to the U.S. and has a high level of organized crime activity with at least four cartels — designated as terrorist organizations by the Trump administration — operating in the region. Besides trafficking drugs, cartels also make money through extortion, including of the avocado industry.

Michoacan State Security Secretary Antonio Cruz told The Associated Press that one of the arrests mentioned by the governor was of “El Poncho,” the alias of Alfonso Fernández Magallón, leader of a local cartel operating in the avocado-growing region around Los Reyes.

U.S. Ambassador to Mexico Ronald Johnson welcomed the arrest, which came over the weekend. The U.S. government had offered a $5 million reward for Fernández Magallón’s arrest.

Cruz said his department was unaware of any direct incidents involving the avocado inspectors. Nevertheless, 300 security personnel were deployed to the Los Reyes area as a preventive measure.

The governor said the priority was to “ensure the security conditions necessary for these operations to resume normally,” as has happened in the past.

Mexico supplies approximately 80% of U.S. avocado imports - a product known in the region as “green gold.” Its cultivation generates around 200,000 jobs in Michoacán alone.

In 2025, Mexico sold $3.65 billion worth of avocados to the United States, and in the first four months of this year, those exports rose by 35% compared to the same period in the previous year.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture sends inspectors in Mexico to monitor plantations and packing houses to ensure that exported produce is free of pests. Threats and violence against the inspectors have caused the U.S. to suspend inspections in the past.

Malaysian durian orchard owner Stephen Chow’s workers spend hours in the fields in the dead of night, donning headlamps to collect freshly ripened fruit coveted by Chinese consumers. But the hard work may not be enough to keep Chow out of the red.

Durian lovers prize the Malaysian premium varieties such as Musang King and Black Thorn, but their growers face a harsher reality. Climate change, caused by the burning of oil, gas and coal, is making it costlier for growers like Chow to produce quality durians, adding pressure as they compete with Thailand and Vietnam, which dominate a booming export market to China.

Extreme weather has dealt repeated blows to Chow’s orchard, which is in Karak, a small town about an hour drive from Kuala Lumpur. In 2021, heavy rainfall triggered flooding that damaged about 100 of his durian trees and his machinery. Over the following three years, persistent rain during flowering season caused pollination failure, cutting into his yield. And now, Chow is facing other challenges.

“Breaking even would already be very good. Most likely there’ll be a loss this year,” Chow said.

Between February and April, afternoon temperatures hit 33 to 35 degrees Celsius (91 to 95 degrees Fahrenheit), and rain fell mostly at night, he said. Such weather favored flowering, and Chow responded by pruning to prevent deformed or small fruit while stepping up watering and fertilization because of the heat. A rise in fuel and fertilizer prices because of the Iran war, however, meant those extra efforts came at a higher cost.

An oversupply of durians in Malaysia — driven by hot and dry weather and more orchards reaching maturity — also pushed prices down. Grade A Musang King durians from his orchard sold for the equivalent of $8.6 per kilogram (about 2.2 pounds) in local currency in early July, about half compared to the same period last year and roughly one-third of the peak price in 2024.

China's love for durians fueled boom

Durians' overpowering smell is fragrant to those who love it and foul to those who don't. Beneath a spiky shell, their flesh offers a rich, creamy texture with varying flavors. Some taste like sweet custard with fruity flourishes, others carry a hint of bitterness, an alcohol tinge or even a peanut butter-like flavor.

Official data showed Malaysia's durian crop covered 92,100 hectares (227,600 acres) in 2024, up almost 40% from 2016, a size even larger than the total land area of Singapore, the city-state island just south of Malaysia. During that period, Malaysia's production grew nearly 90% to 568,800 tonnes.

The boom was fueled by China beginning to import whole frozen Malaysian durians in 2019. Fresh durians followed in 2024, as Beijing expanded what has been dubbed “durian diplomacy” by welcoming more Southeast Asian countries to export the fruit.

The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations said China procured about 95% of global durian exports between 2020 and 2022. It imported 1.87 million tonnes of fresh durians worth $7.5 billion in 2025, with the volume jumping six times in the past decade, according to China's customs data.

Consumers there can find the fruit in supermarkets, grocery stores and durian specialty shops. Shanghai resident Song Xiaohua, in her 30s, said she would eat durians once a week instead of once a month if it weren’t for its high calorie count. To her, durians taste creamy and are like both fruit and dessert.

“It feels like celebrating Lunar New Year every time I have a durian,” Song said.

Malaysia lags far behind Thailand and Vietnam in exports to China. But the Malaysian industry touts its durians as higher quality. Unlike their counterparts, Malaysian growers typically do not harvest early, instead collecting only naturally ripened fruit.

Delivering quality durians requires resilience

As global average temperatures rise, extreme weather events like heat waves, floods and droughts are becoming more frequent and intense worldwide, often forcing farmers to scramble to adapt.

Peninsular Malaysia recorded a significant jump in average temperature from 1969 to 2025, with an increase of 0.24 degrees Celsius (about 0.43 degrees Fahrenheit) per decade, according to the country's meteorological department.

Ooi Teik Hock, whose orchard in Perak state is near the border with Thailand, said there were fewer fruit quality problems when temperatures were lower two decades ago. Concerned about the heat, he moved his orchard from the plains to the highlands about 10 years ago, where nights are cooler and air is more humid.

Still, global warming remains a threat, fueling the proliferation of once-rare pests and forcing Ooi to use pesticides more frequently, which he said have jumped some 30% in price from three years ago.

For the first time, Ooi didn't see fruit bats, a main pollinator, at his orchard during this year's flowering season. He said it could be a result of extreme heat or the widespread use of pesticides for pest and disease control.

The weather changes also affect overall quality, especially for the Musang King variety, which is sensitive to weather conditions, said Lim Chin Khee, an adviser to the Durian Academy, which trains durian growers in Malaysia.

Too much rain during the fruit's rapid development period can cause white and grayish patches on golden yellow flesh, while water shortages during that time can cause some black spots around the flesh, he said.

Some growers turn to technology

With expectations that El Nino, a periodic warming of Pacific Ocean that leads to warmer temperatures, could bring Malaysia record-high temperatures between March and May, Lim advised farmers to expand water reservoirs or prepare to install tube wells as a backup if their ponds dried up.

He said producing good fruit depends equally on the weather and the farmer’s effort. And that extreme weather events would reduce supply while simultaneously driving up prices, he said.

“So for those farmers (who) are well prepared, actually when any disaster strikes, that is an opportunity,” he said.

Grower Kie Kim Hwa learned how to farm durians from his grandfather at a young age. When he took charge of the orchard in Penang Island off Malaysia's western coast, he chose to do things slightly differently than previous generations.

He installed sensors and instruments to track rainfall, humidity and wind speed, among other data, which was sent to a cloud drive for him to review anywhere and keep a record. Some were placed among the trees and grass, and others deep in the soil. Not everything required high technology: he also checked the surface of a bucket of water for insects to gauge pest levels.

The data allowed Kie to intervene early before problems arose and ultimately control fruit quality and quantity to match market demand.

“We live and die by the weather,” he said. “But we can still prepare.”

___

Associated Press writer Fu Ting in Washington contributed to this report.

Mike Lindell has stepped down as CEO of his bedding company, MyPillow, to focus on his run for Minnesota governor.

“Today, I’ve made one of the biggest decisions of my life. I'm stepping down as CEO of MyPillow so I can devote 100% of my time and energy to my campaign for Governor of Minnesota,” Lindell, who founded the company in 2004, wrote on X Tuesday.

“Minnesota deserves my full attention, and that's exactly what I'm giving it. I'm all in, and I can't wait to earn your vote,” he added.

Lindell, a Minnesota native, announced late last year that he would enter the gubernatorial race. Earlier this month, President Donald Trump gave Lindell his endorsement, calling him “one of America’s greatest and most hard working Patriots.”

open image in gallery Mike Lindell has stepped down as CEO of his bedding company MyPillow so he can focus on his run for Minnesota governor ( Getty Images )

At an event for Minnesota’s farmers, Lindell name-dropped Trump, telling the audience of his opponents, “ I have an advantage over everyone up here. I can call up and work with the president of the United States.”

With Lindell gone, Jim Furlong, who served as the company’s president from 2004 to 2019, will return as CEO.

“Real leadership means knowing when to lead, when to trust your team, and when to put a larger calling first,” Lindell said in a press release. “I trust Jim and the Board to protect our employees, our customers, and our Minnesota roots.”

The company has promised that no Minnesota jobs will be affected by the change in leadership.

open image in gallery ‘Minnesota deserves my full attention, and that's exactly what I'm giving it,’ the pro-Trump CEO said ( AFP via Getty Images )

Aside from his MyPillow product, Lindell is known for spreading baseless conspiracy theories about the 2020 presidential election.

In September 2025, a federal judge in Minnesota ruled that Lindell defamed election technology firm Smartmatic by falsely claiming its voting machines helped rig the election.

Last month, it was reported that Lindell settled a $1.3 billion defamation lawsuit that another election tech company formerly known as Dominion Voting Systems filed against him in 2021 over his 2020 conspiracy theories.

In his Truth Social post announcing his support for Lindell, Trump, who continues to baselessly claim that former President Joe Biden stole the 2020 election from him, wrote, “Nobody has sacrificed more than Mike Lindell in fighting for our country, especially when it comes to Election Integrity.”

open image in gallery Aside from his MyPillow product, Lindell is known for spreading baseless conspiracy theories about the 2020 presidential election ( Getty Images )

Minnesota’s Republican and Democratic primary elections for governor will take place Tuesday.

Lindell is leading his Republican opponents by nine points in a recent KSTP/SurveyUSA poll. The MyPillow founder has 35 percent support from likely Republican primary voters, while Minnesota state Representative Lisa Demuth has 26 percent and businessman Kendall Qualls has 11 percent.

The biggest name in the Democratic primary is US Senator Amy Klobuchar.

Current Minnesota Governor Tim Walz abruptly announced in January that he would not seek re-election amid scrutiny of his handling of welfare fraud in the state.

In his statement announcing that he would no longer seek a third term, Walz defended his work to root out fraud: “We’ve gone to the legislature time and again to get more tools to combat fraud. We’ve fired people who weren’t doing their jobs. We’ve seen people go to jail for stealing from our state.”

The Trump administration said Wednesday it will shut down a Kentucky organ donation group accused of continuing plans for organ retrieval from some patients who unexpectedly showed signs of life.

While those surgeries were canceled, the cases made headlines several years ago, prompting a spike in people around the country revoking their organ donor registrations.

Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. called the nonprofit Network for Hope “a bad apple” and accused it of “persistent safety failures” in announcing the government was starting the process to decertify it.

Network for Hope is one of about 55 organ procurement organizations, or OPOs, that coordinate the recovery of organs from deceased donors and help match them to patients on the nation’s transplant list. In a statement, Network for Hope said it “strongly disagrees” with Kennedy’s decision and will appeal.

Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. called the nonprofit Network for Hope ‘a bad apple’ ( Heather Diehl/Getty Images )

Among the allegations is that in 2021, Network for Hope’s predecessor organization pressured a local hospital to proceed with plans to withdraw life support and retrieve organs from a man despite signs that he was waking up from a drug overdose. The man survived and his sister joined Kennedy at a press briefing Wednesday, thanking him.

OPOs cannot declare if someone is dead — only a doctor at the hospital treating the person can do that. Only after that declaration can a donor agency assume responsibility for the deceased, looking for potential recipients and scheduling surgeons to come in to retrieve the organs. Most donations come from people declared brain-dead. But sometimes doctors say a patient has a nonsurvivable injury and the family decides to withdraw life support — and in certain circumstances, that also can allow for donation.

In its statement, Network for Hope said it complies with all federal organ policies. It said that over a year ago it implemented a “first-of-its-kind” new safeguard allowing anyone — including health professionals or family members — to call a pause in donation planning if there’s any concern the patient won’t be appropriate.

Kentucky recently passed a law mandating that pause and the federal Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network is working on new rules that also would require all the nation’s OPOs to implement it.

More than 100,000 people are on the U.S. transplant list, the vast majority seeking a kidney, and thousands will die waiting for a new organ. There were more than 49,000 transplants last year, a record despite a small drop in donations from the deceased — the first such dip in a decade.

FIFA said Wednesday it had apologized for errors made over Gianni Infantino’s failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and that senior staff in attendance at a crisis meeting in Morocco “reaffirmed their full support” for his presidency.

World soccer's governing body attempted to present a unified front amid the turbulence caused by Infantino's controversial plans, with calls for him to step down.

In a statement, FIFA said Secretary-General Mattias Grafström and members of the management board in attendance in Rabat had given their support to the embattled president.

Referring to the plans to sell profits in the World Cup through a commercial subsidiary called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), the statement said “mistakes made were acknowledged” and that the “process should have been handled differently."

FIFA said a letter had been sent to FIFA Council and member associations apologizing for errors and committed to “ensure they do not happen again.”

Grafström’s stated support was notable after he distanced himself from Infantino’s now abandoned plans in an email to all FIFA staff calling the last week a “sad and reproachable series of events.”

FIFA said Infantino had also reaffirmed his support for his secretary general.

World soccer’s governing body said the FFE proposal was “now off the table.”

“There are always lessons to be learned, and FIFA will continue to improve its processes in light of this experience,” it said.

‘Serious questions’

Earlier Wednesday, the association of European soccer leagues — including the Premier League, La Liga and Serie A — called for governance reform of FIFA. It described the FFE proposal as “dangerous” and said it pointed to deeper concerns about how the governing body operates.

It said it raised “serious questions about FIFA’s governance, internal culture and decision-making.”

“Now more than ever, FIFA requires governance reform that ensures that all relevant stakeholders have a formal role in decisions that shape the future of our game.”

In the statement, European Leagues hit out at the possibility of further expanding the World Cup to 64 teams and said “FIFA must not be allowed to continue taking unilaterally disruptive decisions.”

It said that until there was reform it would reject the “expansion or creation” of FIFA competitions.

Portugal and Real Madrid great Luis Figo also called for Infantino to step down, saying he had “debased the office.”

FIFA denied a British media report suggesting Infantino, in seeking support for his presidency, had offered Morocco the hosting of the final at the 2030 World Cup. Spain, Portugal and Morocco are the main co-hosts for the 2030 edition. Morocco hopes to host the final at the planned 115,000-seat King Hassan II Stadium near Casablanca; Spain has at least two contenders — the home stadiums of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

A FIFA spokesperson said it’s “false and misleading to claim the FIFA president has made any promise in relation to hosting the FIFA World Cup 2030 final. A decision will be made by FIFA in due course.”

Canada’s Carney raises concerns

Also Wednesday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he no longer has confidence in Infantino. He said the FIFA president committed a “fatal” governance failure by not consulting senior advisers.

“Certainly I don’t have confidence in Mr. Infantino,” said Carney, who had appeared alongside Infantino at several events during the 2026 World Cup co-hosted by Canada, Mexico and the United States.

A tumultuous week have raised questions about Infantino’s presidency of FIFA ahead of elections in March.

European soccer’s governing body UEFA has applied the most intense pressure by voting to boycott the World Cup if Infantino pressed ahead with FFE.

Even after Infantino’s climbdown UEFA said it had lost confidence in FIFA’s leadership — possibly paving the way for a challenge to his presidency. The governing body for North and Central American and Caribbean soccer (CONCACAF) also said FIFA leadership had “stopped putting football first.”

There have also been signs of division within the organization with chief of global football development Arsène Wenger distancing himself from the FFE plans. Infantino’s senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigned last week and chief operating officer Kevin Lamour said staff were “deceived” by the president’s lack of openness.

Infantino is aiming to win a fourth and final term in office at the March elections.

News.title: Three charged with threats linked to Nolan Wells investigation
News.content:

Three people have been charged with threatening a judge, a witness and local officials involved in the investigation into the death of Nolan Xavier Wells, an 18-year-old who was found dead after a July Fourth boat trip with friends to an island off Mississippi’s Gulf Coast.

The three individuals do not appear to have any connection to Wells, his family, the group he was with or the investigation itself. The threats emerged amid widespread speculation and heightened scrutiny surrounding the case, fueled by unanswered questions about Wells’ final hours, mistrust of law enforcement and Mississippi’s history of racial violence.

Wells, who was Black, had traveled to the uninhabited island with several white classmates from his high school. He did not return to the mainland with the group that night, and his body was discovered two days later in waters near the island.

Authorities have not announced any arrests or identified suspects in Wells’ death. An independent autopsy requested by his family determined his cause of death was “undetermined” pending further investigation.

An independent autopsy commissioned by Wells’ family found the 18-year-old’s cause of death to be ‘undetermined’ pending further investigation ( AP Photo/John Amis )

Attempts to reach the defendants for comment were unsuccessful. Phone numbers listed for some of the defendants in affidavits weren't active and a call to another number went unanswered. Emails sent to addresses listed in an affidavit for one of the defendants went unanswered. It is unclear if they have attorneys yet.

One of the defendants, Edward James Porter of Illinois, allegedly called an unnamed witness on July 31 and threatened to kill them and their family, according to an affidavit. Porter also allegedly told another person in Mississippi in a phone call that he would cut them up and put them “into a suitcase.” Porter was charged on July 31 in federal court for the Southern District of Mississippi for the threat.

Porter threatened two members of the family of Bart Edminston Jr., a 21-year-old who knew Wells and provided aid to the boat the group used on July Fourth, said family attorney Russell Latino. Latino said that one of the family members who Porter threatened is a witness in the investigation into Wells’ death.

An Ohio woman was also charged with allegedly placing bomb threats at the George County Chancery Clerk's Office and the Jackson County Sheriff’s Office on July 23. The woman, Michelle Francine Edwards, allegedly called the clerk's office 21 times and said, “the clock is ticking,” according to an affidavit.

A California man, Joseph Alfredo Vasquez Dumarce, was charged on July 14 for allegedly sending a threatening Facebook message to a Jackson County Chancery Court judge with ties to the Wells investigation. According to an affidavit, a Facebook user believed to be Dumarce sent a message to the judge's account that constituted a “threat that a bomb would be mailed to the judge's office."

Judge Ashlee Cole posted a screenshot of Dumarce's threatening message on Facebook on July 9. Cole wrote in an earlier Facebook post that her son last saw Wells on July Fourth around 3 p.m. and decided to “stay on the island and return inland later with another group of friends.” Cole wrote that she deactivated her Facebook and that she fears for the safety of her children.

“No one in our family is trying in any way to impede with the investigation by law enforcement or to otherwise hamper the family and law enforcement’s quest for answers,” Cole wrote, adding that her son “cooperated fully” with the sheriff's investigation. ___ Kelety reported from Phoenix. Associated Press journalist Sophie Bates in Jackson, Mississippi, contributed.

Los Angeles County health officials have issued a public health alert after an individual with an infectious case of measles visited Universal Studios Hollywood last month, potentially exposing numerous park-goers to the highly contagious virus.

The Los Angeles County Department of Public Health confirmed that anyone present at the theme park on Sunday, July 26, between 10 a.m. and 9 p.m., may have been exposed.

Officials are currently investigating other potential exposure sites. Individuals who visited during this timeframe are advised to monitor themselves for symptoms until August 16.

While those who have previously contracted measles or received the recommended measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine are generally protected, health officials still recommend vigilance for symptoms. Unvaccinated individuals or those with an unknown vaccination status face a significantly higher risk of infection.

Unvaccinated individuals or those with an unknown vaccination status face a significantly higher risk of infection ( Jan Sonnenmair/Getty Images )

"As measles cases increase, it is important that residents take steps to make sure they are fully protected," Los Angeles County Health Officer Dr. Muntu Davis said in a statement. "The MMR vaccine is the safest and most reliable way to prevent measles and protect yourself, your family and your community."

Health officials urged residents to review their vaccination records, particularly before traveling, and to contact a health care provider if they are pregnant, immunocompromised, have an infant younger than 12 months who may have been exposed or are otherwise at higher risk.

Anyone who develops symptoms including fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes or a rash should stay home, avoid school, work and public gatherings, and contact a health care provider before visiting a medical facility, officials said.

Measles spreads through the air when an infected person breathes, talks, coughs or sneezes, and the virus can remain in the air or on surfaces for several hours after the infected person has left an area. According to the department, two doses of the MMR vaccine are about 97 percent effective at preventing the disease.

As of July 31, 2,371 measles cases have been reported nationwide this year, according to county health officials. Most of the cases are linked to outbreaks that began in 2025 and 2026. Los Angeles County last reported a measles case on July 21.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino issues grovelling apology for botched World Cup plot after crisis meeting
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino issues grovelling apology for botched World Cup plot after crisis meeting

Gianni Infantino has been under fire for the last week after FIFA's controversial plan to sell off its competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors came to light

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been forced to apologise (Image: Tasos Katopodis - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Grovelling Gianni Infantino has apologised for attempting to sell the World Cup, confirming that the controversial plan has been SCRAPPED. Infantino has faced intense backlash since FIFA announced last week - after media reports broke the news - a proposal for its competitions to be sold to private investors, sparking anger among the football community at all levels.

‌



UEFA members unanimously voted to boycott FIFA tournaments if the plan was allowed to go ahead, while FIFA chief Arsene Wenger spoke out against it. A crisis meeting was held in Morocco on Wednesday amid the unrelenting criticism and constant leaks regarding the plans.

‌



And now Infantino has admitted defeat with an apology - although he plans to fight on and remain FIFA President, despite widespread calls for him to resign. A letter signed by both Infantino and the FIFA General Secretary, Mattias Grafstrom, reads: "We acknowledge that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media.

‌



"We sincerely apologise for these errors and commit to them not happening again. With this in mind, we will conduct a necessary review, and a report will be presented to the FIFA Council at its next scheduled meeting."

It goes on to say: "With the project withdrawn, FIFA will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation."

‌



Meanwhile, FIFA say that its leadership held a constructive and positive meeting in Rabat. It comes after a bombshell report claiming that Infantino had offered Morocco the chance to host 2030 World Cup final - which they're co-hosting with Spain and Portugal - if they agreed to his plan.

Sports.title: Rusty Arsenal suffer friendly defeat as Mikel Arteta dealt injury blow - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Rusty Arsenal suffer friendly defeat as Mikel Arteta dealt injury blow - 5 talking points

ARSENAL 1-3 REAL BETIS: The Gunners were convincingly beaten in Dublin, giving Mikel Arteta some cause for concern ahead of his team's season which starts in just 11 days' time

View 5 Images Mikel Arteta will be disappointed with Arsenal's result and performance (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

Lacklustre Arsenal fell to a comprehensive 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in their second pre-season friendly. The Gunners gave their fans in Dublin little to enjoy with an under-par display.

‌



Mikel Arteta watched his side make a string of mistakes, showing the kind of rustiness that he'll hope will be gone in less than a fortnight when they start the 2026-27 season against Manchester City for the Community Shield. Arsenal found themsleves 2-0 down inside 26 minutes and Arteta was visibly frustrated on the touchline.

‌



Piero Hincapie pulled one back but Betis didn't take long to restore their two-goal advantage before half-time. A raft of changes didn't make much difference in the second half and it was a match that will have fans talking for the wrong reasons.

‌



Here are five talking points from the Aviva Stadium.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Real Madrid change Vinicius Jr stance as Arsenal transfer hopes suffer blow READ MORE :

1. Kepa's clangers

With Illan Meslier through the door, there's competition to be Arsenal's No.2 goalkeeper. But Kepa Arrizabalaga didn't help his case by making an error in the ninth minute.

‌



A corner was floated in by Pablo Fornals and Kepa came steaming out looking to punch. But the Spaniard got it all wrong and completely missed the ball, giving Rodrigo Riquelme a tap-in.

Kepa's appeals for a foul fell on deaf ears and soon enough he made another error. His poor clearance surrendered possession to Betis and Nelson Deossa punished him with an unstoppable strike.

Will Arsenal win the Premier League? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 5 Images Arsenal got off to a nightmare start (Image: Evan Treacy/Getty Images)

2. Still Set Piece FC

After finding themselves 2-0 down and playing poorly, Arsenal needed a response. That came in the form of - you guessed it - a corner.

New signing Christos Tzolis whipped the ball in and it evaded flapping Betis goalkeeper Alvaro Valles inside his own six-yard box. Standing a matter of inches from the line, Hincapie had a simple task to nod the ball in.

‌



It was another well-worked routine from the Gunners. Tzolis' delivery dipped perfectly and Betis were bamboozled by the runners in yellow, who were sporting Arsenal's new third kit.

View 5 Images Piero Hincapie pulled a goal back from a corner (Image: Paul Faith/AFP via Getty Images)

3. Guimaraes required

On the day Arsenal agreed a £75million deal to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle, their second-choice midfield was exposed. Sloppy, lethargic, careless - all of those could be thrown at the trio of Ethan Nwaneri, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Kai Havertz.

‌



Both Betis' second and third goals summed up their performances that will remind the Arsenal board just why they're buying Guimaraes. Deossa's strike may've been a screamer but he was afforded was too much time to pull the trigger.

And then for Fornals' goal which restored Betis' two-goal cushion, Havertz gave the ball away with a weak pass. It was all far too easy and so unlike Arsenal.

View 5 Images Kai Havertz's mistake proved costly (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

‌



4. Injury blow for teenager

Arteta rung in the changes at half-time, making a total of seven substitutions. One who came on was Louie Copley, who captained Arsenal's under-21 side last season aged 19.

But sadly for the highly-rated midfielder, who was used at right-back, his night only last 10 minutes. Copley had landed awkwardly while chasing the ball and immediately looked in pain.

Arteta reluctantly subbed him, as the teenager had to be helped off the pitch as he struggled to put weight on his leg. Hopefully for Copley, it's nothing serious.

‌



View 5 Images Louie Copley succumbed to injury 10 minutes after coming on (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

5. Arteta managing minutes

As the game petered out, albeit with Betis looking the more likely to score against a youth Arsenal XI, Arteta made two intriguing substitutions. Gabriel Magalhaes and Gabriel Martinelli had only entered the fray at half-time, but they came off 30 minutes later.

The two Brazilians had only reached the round of 16 at the World Cup, but it's clear that Arteta is being careful with his starters who played a mammoth amount of minutes last season. Both Gabriels should be involved on Saturday at home to Borussia Dortmund.

Sports.title: Newcastle finally confirm Matthias Jaissle as new manager to replace Eddie Howe
Sports.content:
Newcastle finally confirm Matthias Jaissle as new manager to replace Eddie Howe

Newcastle quickly identified Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle as their top target to replace Eddie Howe, but the announcement of his appointment was delayed - until now

View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle has been confirmed by Newcastle (Image: FC Red Bull Salzburg via Getty Images)

Newcastle have finally confirmed the appointment of Matthias Jaissle as their new manager. Jaissle, 38, arrives from Saudi Arabian club Al-Ahli, with Newcastle paying a £9.5million compensation fee.

‌



The German replaces Eddie Howe, who shockingly resigned midway through pre-season last week. Jaissle has already been working with Newcastle's squad in La Manga, Spain for the last few days.

‌



But Al-Ahli wanted to delay the announcement until 7pm on Wednesday. Jaissle spent three years in Saudi Arabia following spells with Red Bull Salzburg and Liefering in Austria.

‌



The 38-year-old guided Al-Ahli - who are owned by Newcastle's owners, the Saudi Public Investment Fund - to winning the Asian Champions League in each of the last two seasons. But Jaissle has decided to move to St James' Park, kicking off a new era.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill in hospital as club issue health update READ MORE :

"When Newcastle United comes your way, you take notice," he commented in Newcastle's announcement. "The ambition of the club, the vision for the future and the opportunity ahead made this an incredibly compelling place to be.

‌



"I have followed the club's journey closely in recent years and the progress that has been made is clear for everyone to see. I am incredibly excited about the future. I fully and unreservedly believe in this project, the ambition and the direction the club is taking.

"There is a clear vision, strong leadership and an exceptional platform to build on. My teams are built on togetherness, hard work, intensity and a passion to improve every single day.

"I will bring full commitment, full energy and a determination to give everything I have to help this club achieve its ambitions. I believe there is enormous potential within this squad and throughout the football club.

‌



Will Matthias Jaissle be a success at Newcastle? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle won the Asian Champions League twice (Image: Getty Images)

"I am excited to work with the players, staff and leadership team to help take the club forward. I cannot wait to get started and will attack this opportunity. I give my complete commitment and total energy to bringing further success to Newcastle United."

‌



Sporting director Ross Wilson added: "Matthias' leadership style and football philosophy are strongly aligned with our sporting vision. His teams play high-energy football and we could feel his passion during all of our discussions throughout the recruitment process.

"He has consistently demonstrated an ability to improve players, build cohesive teams and create elite performance environments in his coaching career.

"His successes at Salzburg and Al-Ahli underline his ability to deliver results while developing a clear football identity. We believe he is uniquely positioned to build on the strong foundations already in place and help take Newcastle United forward."

Jaissle's first Premier League game in charge will be at home to Liverpool on Sunday, August 23.

Sports.title: Real Madrid change Vinicius Jr stance as Arsenal transfer hopes suffer blow
Sports.content:
Real Madrid change Vinicius Jr stance as Arsenal transfer hopes suffer blow

Real Madrid are continuing to hold talks with Vinicius Jr and his entourage, while Arsenal are waiting in the wings hoping to pull off a sensational transfer swoop

View 2 Images Arsenal are going all out to sign Vinicius Junior (Image: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Real Madrid have made Vinicius Jr an improved contract offer in a bid to fend off interest from Arsenal. Vinicius, 26, has entered the final year of his current deal in Madrid and the Gunners are willing to offer him a lucrative move to London.

‌



Arsenal would be willing to make the Brazilian their highest-paid player and boss Mikel Arteta is believed to have spoken to him. On Wednesday, talks between Vinicius' camp, Real general director Jose Angel Sanchez and chief scout Juni Calafat took place.

‌



The two parties had previously been far apart in negotiations, with Vinicius demanding an eye-watering salary of €28m (£24m). According to The Athletic, Real have now raised their offer to a level which they believe reflects the forward's importance.

‌



Vinicius' decision on the proposal will either bring an end to the saga over his future or let it rumble on. Should no agreement be found, Real would have to decide whether to sell him this summer or risk letting him leave as a free agent next year.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer READ MORE :

If Vinicius does stay at the La Liga giants, he'll be owed a substantial loyalty bonus which is reportedly worth around £9m. New Real manager Jose Mourinho wants the 26-year-old to stay, as he aims to make a successful return to the Bernabeu.

On Tuesday, Vinicius gave an interview to Real Madrid TV about working under Mourinho. "It has ⁠gone very well, getting to know the new coach and the new players, and training very hard," he said. "Mourinho wants me to be as I have always been: happy, cheerful ‌and playing my football."

Mikel Arteta could be asked about Arsenal's pursuit of Vinicius when his side face Real Betis in a friendly in Dublin on Wednesday. It comes after Arsenal agreed a £75m deal with Newcastle for Bruno Guimaraes, Vinicius' international team-mate.

‌



The Gunners beat Girona 4-1 in their opening pre-season friendly thanks to goals from Kai Havertz, Christos Tzolis, Max Dowman and Gabriel Jesus. Tszolis remains Arsenal's only outfield signing so far, with the Greek winger joining from Club Brugge for £34m.

Will Vinicius Jr stay or go? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Real Madrid's offer is bad news for Arsenal (Image: Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

‌



Arteta has also welcomed a new goalkeeper. French shot-stopper Illan Meslier arrived on a free transfer, having been released by Leeds.

After playing Betis, Arsenal will host two friendlies at the Emirates against Borussia Dortmund and Como. Their first game of the season will be the Community Shield against Manchester City, who Arsenal pipped to the Premier League title last term.

The Gunners kick-off their league campaign by facing newly-promoted Coventry at home on Friday, August 21. Arteta's side then travel to Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Arsenal 'prepare second offer' for England star as Morgan Rogers deal causes complication
Sports.content:
Arsenal 'prepare second offer' for England star as Morgan Rogers deal causes complication

Arsenal are looking to formalise their pursuit of a third marquee signing of the summer window in addition to Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Jr

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa is still wanted by Arsenal but a Morgan Rogers transfer problem could be repeated (Image: (Photo by Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images))

Aston Villa are expecting Arsenal to submit a second offer for Ezri Konsa after an opening bid fell short of their £60million valuation. Sporting director Andrea Berta is believed to be looking at potential defensive signings due to William Saliba's back injury that is expected to keep him out for several months.

‌



Konsa emerged as an option for Arsenal in July following a strong season at Villa Park. During the World Cup, a 'low-ball offer' was lodged to Villa and was quickly turned down with it said to have left a sour taste.

‌



His former team-mate Morgan Rogers was of firm interest to the Gunners before he completed a staggering £117m move to Chelsea. The bid for Konsa did not help Arsenal's chances of signing Rogers, and could yet impact Mikel Arteta's side in any deal for the English defender.

‌



How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal, however, are unlikely to give up hope of signing him as per the Daily Mail, who have also claimed that Villa are bracing for a fresh proposal from north London.

Following their first bid, Konsa is said to have remained on Arsenal's radar while Villa are hoping for him to sign a new contract, with his current deal expiring in the summer of 2028.

‌



Having acquired over £150m from selling Rogers and Youri Tielemans, Villa are not under financial pressure to sell. Those key departures also will seemingly harden Unai Emery's stance on Konsa, with an exit unlikely to be sanctioned unless a deal for a suitable replacement is lined up.

View 2 Images Arsenal have tried to sign Aston Villa duo Morgan Rogers and Ezri Konsa this summer

Konsa is entering the final stages of his three-week break following the World Cup. Players that reached the quarter-finals in the tournament have returned this week which has seen two Arsenal deals ramp up.

‌



A deal for Bruno Guimaraes is in the process of being finalised with Newcastle United to receive £75m for their captain.

His fellow Brazilian Vinicius Jr is also being targeted with his Real Madrid future remaining uncertain as he has just 12 months remaining on his current deal.

Completing both of those transfers is seemingly Arsenal's priority this summer, with a pursuit of Konsa expected to be formalised after that - despite the difficulties in getting a deal done for the England defender.

Sports.title: Rockets march on after easy win while Buttler makes history in The Hundred
Sports.content:
Trent Rockets extended their lead at the top of The Hundred table with a near-perfect performance that secured their fifth win in six games, leaving Birmingham Phoenix rooted to the bottom.

Sam Billings' unbeaten 31 sealed a scrappy chase after Phoenix stuttered to 111-6 despite Joe Clarke's 50, while Jos Buttler made history for the Manchester Super Giants as he became the leading Twenty20 run-scorer of all time.

After the Rockets elected to field, Will Smeed broke an unwanted record by being the first batter in The Hundred history to be unbeaten without scoring at the end of the powerplay. 25 runs came from that powerplay for the loss of Mitch Owen to Mohammad Amir, who had to leave the field with a strained hamstring immediately after taking the wicket.

Smeed eventually fell for six off 16 balls, with the visitors appearing tentative against a disciplined attack led by outstanding performances from spinners Calvin Harrison and Mitch Santner, along with Lewis Gregory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A crowd member made a great catch during Trent Rockets match against Birmingham Phoenix

Only Joe Clarke, Phoenix's leading run-scorer this season, managed to break free, reaching a half-century from 37 balls before finishing with 62 off 47. He became the fourth victim of Craig Overton's safe hands, with the catches setting a competition record. Of the remaining batters, only Laurie Evans reached double figures as Phoenix limped to an underwhelming 111-6 from their 100 balls.

After Amir's departure, skipper Billings had juggled his bowlers expertly as he searches for a fourth successive title in The Hundred. And when the Rockets batted, there was little pressure on the openers, Ben Duckett and Finn Allen progressing smoothly to 29-0 in the powerplay.

Mystery spinner Usman Tariq removed Duckett for 22 and delivered his customary bow celebration, conceding just six runs from his first 10 balls. However, there were simply not enough runs on the board, with 113 becoming the lowest total ever successfully defended in The Hundred men's competition.

Nye Donald came and went after a typically pugnacious six-ball 17, before Allen and Billings calmly rotated the strike at around a run a ball. Two successive sixes from Billings off Saqib Mahmood, including an outrageous slog sweep, accelerated the finish, and the result was all but confirmed when Allen holed out to Tariq at short mid-on for 28 with only six runs required.

The Rockets completed the victory with another Billings six, winning with 17 balls to spare to be sitting pretty with two games to come, their route direct to the final having got that bit easier.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Overton makes FOUR great catches for Trent Rockets

Gregory said: "We were superb with the ball. We kept chipping away with important wickets. It was a little bit two-paced, with a bit of variable bounce at times. The bowling unit spoke about smashing the top of the stump as hard as we could.

"The guys up front with the bat have been outstanding. We're in a really good position, playing some fantastic cricket, and hopefully we can continue that."

Buttler become the leading Twenty20 run-scorer of all time

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jos Buttler hits a mega half century to win it for Manchester Super Giants vs Welsh Fire

After three straight defeats, Manchester Super Giants got the win they needed over Welsh Fire at an overcast Emirates Old Trafford to remain in contention for qualification.

Half-centuries from Tim Seifert and Jos Buttler propelling them to a crunching win with 31 balls to spare.

Seifert said: "We just tried to get off to a good start and maintain the run rate and it was good that we both got going. And it was quite nice to watch Buttler from the other end! We've got two big games ahead and this is a good little boost for us."

The Super Giants move up to 12 points, now just four behind the Fire with two games left each.

They had to do it without their captain Aiden Markram, who has returned to South Africa for personal reasons, Jos Buttler taking over captaincy duties and Paul Walter replacing him at the top of the order, meaning there were just three overseas players in the line-up.

Second-placed Fire won the toss and chose to bat, reaching an uncomfortable 4-0 from the first ten balls after Josh Tongue didn't concede a single run off his first five balls.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Leus du Plooy with a big drop catch for the Giants...

Spin was introduced at that stage, with Liam Dawson seeing Matt Short dropped almost immediately. The openers took full advantage, progressing steadily at first before opening up to reach 76 at the halfway stage. Their century partnership - the first in Fire men's history - came up after 70 balls.

Short was particularly severe on Noor Ahmad, who conceded 34 runs from 15 balls, while Sonny Baker was even more expensive. Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue, however, were excellent, with the latter finally breaking the opening partnership at 125 after 83 balls by dismissing Phil Salt for 48. Short went on to make 71 from 47 balls, but with quick runs needed late on, Joe Root was not required at the crease as Fire posted what appeared to be a par score of 155, thanks largely to Rachin Ravindra's late cameo.

Sam Cook was unusually expensive with the ball as the Super Giants began their innings, with openers Tim Seifert and Paul Walter taking a liking to the pace of the Essex seamer, Chris Woakes and Lockie Ferguson as they raced to 53 without loss in the powerplay.

Walter went for 37 but the home side were 104-1 off 50, an extraordinary three no balls in six balls from Ferguson giving them a real boost.

Buttler started cautiously before switching into full attack mode, launching Marco Jansen into the stands to become the leading run-scorer in Twenty20 history, surpassing Kieron Pollard's tally of 14,803 runs. He celebrated the milestone by clearing the ropes in each of the next two balls, before adding further successive sixes to bring up a 20-ball half-century and guide his side home with ease.

Sports.title: Infantino remains FIFA president following crisis meeting
Sports.content:
Under-fire FIFA president Gianni Infantino has shaken off calls to resign - for now - with the backing of the governing body's leaders, though apologised for "mistakes" in his botched attempts to sell off a stake in the World Cup.

In a statement released after seven hours of crisis talks in Morocco, FIFA said its management board had re-affirmed their "full support" for Infantino - including secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, only days after he had labelled the World Cup plans "a sad and reproachable series of events". The pair were later seen laughing together watching a Women's AFCON game in Rabat.

Infantino had faced mounting calls to resign following the leak of previously undiscussed proposals, after it was revealed national associations had not been consulted and had been given a deadline barely a month away in mid-September and the promise of a £30.1m incentive to back them.

In a letter seen by Sky News sent to national associations and signed by Infantino and Grafstrom, the pair wrote that they "sincerely apologised for the errors" in the plans which were eventually withdrawn on Saturday following days of criticism from across world football.

You can change your settings at any time via the Privacy Options Unfortunately we have been unable to verify if you have consented to Twitter cookies. To view this content you can use the button below to allow Twitter cookies for this session only. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once

A second statement released publicly through FIFA.com hit back at those critics, threatening that FIFA would "no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation".

FIFA said it had "not been the intention… for member associations to feel excluded from the process" and admitted they should have been "handled differently" while further acknowledging "errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media."

The governing body also promised a review would be conducted into the fiasco and a report into its findings presented at the next FIFA Council, comprising 37 national representatives from around world football.

Infantino and FIFA's reputation had taken increasing hits from inside and outside of its own walls over the plans with Arsene Wenger, its chief of global football development, distancing himself publicly while Infantino's personal senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro quit his role on Friday, labelling them a "bad deal" and "irresponsible".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports’ Kaveh Solhekol explains whether Gianni Infantino will walk away from FIFA after crisis meeting

The head of the Jordan FA went further by accusing Infantino of "blackmail", while UEFA announced it had "lost confidence in the current FIFA leadership" and the FA called for a "full and robust review of FIFA's leadership".

Those calls had grown further on Wednesday as legendary winger Luis Figo labelled Infantino's actions "the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed" while Canada prime minister Mark Carney - whose country had welcomed Infantino in as World Cup co-hosts only weeks earlier - said the incident should be "fatal" for his position as FIFA president.

FIFA did not address those calls directly and instead said the marathon meeting would "strengthen FIFA's governance, help restore confidence in the organisation and enable us to prepare for the major events and challenges ahead in a united and transparent manner".

What next for Infantino? 'Associations have levers to force him out'

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

Infantino is a man with a very thick skin, obviously he's aware of what is being said about him - but his feeling all along has been that he was elected president by the 211 associations around the world which make up FIFA and if he's going to be removed, it's going to be by them.

The Prime Minister of Canada, Mark Carney, said he's lost confidence in Infantino. That's significant because Canada were one of the three co-hosts at the World Cup this summer, and Carney was at the World Cup final two and a half weeks ago sat near Infantino.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol provides the latest update regarding the ongoing situation with Infantino, as the Football Association is set to withdraw their support for the FIFA president

I don't think him refusing to resign is something all the associations around the world are going to accept after losing faith in him. They have a few other levers they can use to try to force him out.

There could be an emergency FIFA Council with a vote of no confidence, and he would be out if he lost. There could be an emergency FIFA Congress, with the same outcome.

If he wants to cling on and wait until the next presidential election in March, he may feel he has the numbers to get re-elected despite the opposition against him.

The date to look out for in that case is November 18, the deadline for candidates to declare themselves.

He has got his calculator out and still feels he has support in different parts of the world - South America, Africa and parts of Asia. He feels he lives to fight another day.

What were FIFA's World Cup plans?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martyn Ziegler joins the Paper Talk team to discuss Infantino's future at FIFA

Under the initial proposal to launch FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), football's world governing body aimed to raise up to $4.2bn (£3.1bn) from external investors through the sale of minority, non-controlling stakes in FFE, which it said would be valued at around $20bn (£15bn).

The governing body said its plans - which would have required approval from member associations - could deliver more than $10bn in "football development funding" over the next four years.

Who could replace Infantino?

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

There's been talk about the president of Paris Saint-Germain, Nasser Al-Khelaifi, one of the most powerful men in world football, who is on the UEFA executive committee. But my understanding is that he is not interested in replacing Infantino.

Other candidates are people like Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, who came second in the vote to become FIFA president 10 years ago. He's the president of the AFC, who also oppose the sell-off plans.

Then there's the president of CONCACAF, Victor Montagliani. We've just had the World Cup in three CONCACAF countries and historically, CONCACAF have been close to Infantino, but they said on Thursday that they rejected the proposal as well.

Finally, someone I think would be very popular is Aleksander Ceferin, the president of UEFA. He has a totally different vision about the way football should be run. If he was the president of FIFA, there would be no hydration breaks, no FIFA Peace Prizes, no Qatari-owned private jets for the president, no $1m (£742,000) World Cup tickets.

But I don't think Ceferin has ever expressed any desire or interest publicly to replace Infantino.

Perhaps we are getting ahead of ourselves. Infantino is under a lot of pressure and it would be fair to say he is fighting for his job, but we are not at the stage where people are going to come out and say they are going to stand against him.

Sports.title: Castleford head coach Carr to miss the game against Hull KR
Sports.content:
Castleford Tigers head coach Ryan Carr will not be in attendance at the Hull KR game due to personal reasons.

Chris Chester, Scott Murrell and Rob Nickolay will lead the team in his absence and they will be supported by club legend and Man of Steel Adrian Vowles.

Australian Carr took charge in pre-season on a three-year deal having previously been coach of Featherstone Rovers and assistant manager at Leeds Rhinos in 2019.

A statement released by the club read: "Castleford Tigers RLFC can confirm that head coach Ryan Carr will not be in attendance at the Hull KR game this coming Friday. We can confirm that this is due to personal reasons, contrary to the reports on social media.

"In the interim, Chris Chester, Rob Nickolay and Scott Murrell will lead our on and off field operations. This leadership group will be heavily supported by Adrian Vowles and we thank Adrian for offering his support at short notice.

"We will not be making any other further comment at this stage, and we urge our fans to once again get behind our team this coming Friday."

Castleford currently sit ninth in the Super League table with seven wins from 21 games.

With six games remaining in the season, they face the Robins followed by Hull FC, St Helens, Catalans Dragons, Bradford Bulls, and Huddersfield Giants.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

Sports.title: Arsenal beaten by Real Betis in Dublin friendly
Sports.content:
Arsenal produced a sloppy performance as they were beaten 3-1 by LaLiga side Real Betis in a pre-season friendly in Dublin.

The Gunners fell behind when Kepa Arrizabalaga came out and failed to claim a corner, allowing Rodrigo Riquelme to score at the back post. Nelson Deossa added a stunning second from long range.

Arsenal pulled one back when an inswinging corner from new signing Christos Tzolis was headed over the line by Piero Hincapie but Betis restored their two-goal lead when Pablo Fornals found the bottom corner following a misplaced pass by Kai Havertz.

How did Arsenal line up? Starting XI: Kepa, White, Mosquera, Hincapie, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Nwaneri, Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis



Subbed on: Copley, Salmon, Gabriel, Vieira, Nelson, Jesus, Martinelli, Julienne, Meslier, Ibrahim, Ogunnaike, Clarke, Kabia, O'Neill

Mikel Arteta made second-half changes with Brazil internationals Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli given their first cameos of pre-season but Arsenal, still without Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard and others involved at the World Cup, were unable to cut the deficit.

The defeat, their first of pre-season, comes as Arsenal continue to push for new signings in the transfer market, with the club having agreed a £75m fee with Newcastle for Bruno Guimaraes.
