Sports.title: Robert Garcia Accuses Jaron Ennis Of Targeting Injured Josh Kelly To Avoid Vergil Ortiz Jr.
Sports.content:
“If Boots decides to fight Kelly and take advantage of Kelly being cut and everything, then that’s kind of showing me that you really don’t want to fight Virgil,” Robert said to Sean Zittel. “The fighter will probably do it because he’s a fighter. He’s a warrior, and he’ll probably get the biggest payday in his career, and he could lose to anybody else because, let’s be real, Kelly might not be the best in the division. So, they’re going after him to take advantage of that opportunity to get another belt under his belt.”

The veteran trainer dismissed any suggestion that his fighter needs an interim bout before pursuing the division’s biggest name. Ortiz is already back in camp. He said the former interim champion wants Ennis next.

“We don’t need a tuneup. We want to go straight into Boots,” Garcia said. “If Boots decides to go after him and take advantage of that big old cut, then that’s the way they’re going to do it. I can’t force them either.”

Ennis has repeatedly spoken about adding more world titles, with Kelly and WBC champion Sebastian Fundora mentioned as possible opponents. Garcia rejected that explanation, insisting the larger fight sits across the ring.

“No, that’s a lie. He doesn’t want to fight Virgil,” Garcia said. “The fight against Virgil is three times bigger when it comes to his payday, to a meaningful fight. Nobody’s going to care because you beat Kelly or you beat Virgil. A win over somebody like Virgil means a lot more than Josh Kelly.”

Asked why he believes Ortiz wins the matchup, Garcia offered a brief reply.

“Because I know he beats him,” Garcia said. “I know he beat him.”

Sports.title: Jose Valenzuela Calls For William Zepeda Title Fight
Sports.content:
“Felicidades por la victoria. Sin duda, es otra gran pelea que me encantaría hacer. Ojalá algún día podamos compartir el ring,” Valenzuela wrote on X. Translated, Valenzuela said: “Congratulations on the victory. Without a doubt, it’s another great fight that I’d love to make. Hopefully one day we can share the ring.”

Fresh off his second-round knockout of a ring-rusty Edwin De Los Santos on June 28, Valenzuela (16-3, 10 KOs) is trying to turn that performance into another title opportunity. Before calling for Zepeda, he repeatedly called out fellow Zuffa fighter and WBO light welterweight champion Shakur Stevenson, but those public challenges gained little attention.

Matching Valenzuela with Zepeda presents a different challenge.

Zepeda is promoted by Golden Boy Promotions and competes on DAZN, while Valenzuela is now aligned with Zuffa Boxing and fights on Paramount+. Crossing promotional lines and television platforms is possible, but it usually requires a matchup with significant commercial value.

Unless one side is willing to bridge that promotional divide, Valenzuela may have to keep looking in-house for his next opportunity while Zepeda pursues bigger names at lightweight. Neither promotion has shown interest in working together yet.

Sports.title: Larry Holmes vs. Tex Cobb: A Title Fight That Never Should Have Happened
Sports.content:
The timing could hardly have been worse. Just 13 days earlier, Duk Koo Kim died from injuries sustained in his lightweight title fight with Ray Mancini. Boxing was facing intense criticism over fighter safety, and every televised bout carried added scrutiny. Holmes then defended his WBC heavyweight championship against Randall “Tex” Cobb, a durable pressure fighter whose style played directly into the champion’s strengths.

It took only a few minutes to see how difficult the fight would be. Holmes established his jab immediately, keeping Cobb at the end of his punches while the challenger trudged forward looking for openings that rarely appeared.

Holmes took control almost immediately, repeatedly snapping Cobb’s head back with straight punches while staying comfortably out of danger. Cobb kept marching forward, but each attempt to close the distance brought more punishment than success.

Before long, the championship no longer felt competitive. Cobb’s determination never wavered, yet he had no answer for Holmes’ speed, timing or control of the distance.

Howard Cosell reached that conclusion as the rounds wore on. Working the ABC broadcast, he repeatedly questioned why referee Steve Crosson allowed the fight to continue. Cosell called it a total mismatch and wondered whether the prolonged punishment damaged boxing’s public image. His frustration became one of the night’s defining storylines, and the bout is widely remembered as the final straw that led him to leave professional boxing broadcasts.

Nothing about the performance was reckless. Holmes avoided unnecessary risks and dominated virtually every round. Cobb spent most of the fight trying to get inside, only to run into the jab again and again.

Yet that same superiority turned the fight into an ordeal for many viewers. Every clean jab and unanswered combination reinforced the same question: when does a championship fight stop being competitive enough to continue?

After 15 rounds, the scorecards reflected the one-sided action. Holmes retained his title by unanimous decision. Cobb never touched the canvas despite absorbing hundreds of punches. His courage was beyond question, though the wisdom of allowing him to remain in the fight drew severe scrutiny.

Holmes-Cobb became far more than another title defense. It showed what can happen when a champion operates on a completely different level from his challenger. Coming less than two weeks after Duk Koo Kim’s death, the fight also renewed questions about when a referee should stop a one-sided beating.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Reveals Private Conversation With Devin Haney
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez already has a long-term target in mind beyond his August 22 challenge for Rolando Romero’s WBA welterweight title. The former two-division champion revealed he recently spoke with Devin Haney and believes the pair are on separate courses toward an eventual fight for the undisputed welterweight championship.

“I told Devin Haney about this,” Teofimo said to Sean Zittel. “I told Devin Haney, ‘Me and you, we’re going to go two different sides, but we’re going to meet at the end for undisputed at once.’ He said, ‘All right, those are your words.’ I said, ‘I’m keeping them. Let’s get it going.’ So, I think right now it’s more so who wins September 12th, but mainly right now focus on August 22nd. We’ll go from there. I don’t think I’m going to see Haney until the end.”

Lopez made it clear he is in no rush to face Haney. His preference is for both champions to continue collecting titles before meeting with every major belt on the line.



Teofimo also believes he will be a better fighter by the time that meeting arrives. Asked if he can eventually solve Haney’s movement and back-foot style, he expressed no doubts. “Absolutely. You just got to practice. You got to practice on all those fundamentals. That’s it. I’m a pure boxer when it comes to it,” said Teofimo. “Coming forward has been looked at as a flaw of mine, but flaws are meant to happen so that you can fix them.” Teofimo has repeatedly identified becoming the undisputed welterweight champion before the 2028 Olympic Games as one of his biggest career goals. Rolly remains the immediate obstacle, while Haney continues building his own position atop the division. If both champions continue winning over the next several years, Lopez believes he and Haney will eventually meet in one of the biggest fights available at 147 pounds. Share via: Facebook

Sports.title: Staging Joshua vs. Fury in New York Is a Massive Streaming Gamble
Sports.content:
The strategy hinges on an ambitious corporate thesis: streaming platforms need live events that capture prime-time American viewership. By staging the event on a Friday night in Manhattan, Netflix can target prime-time viewers across North and South America while treating the British audience as a secondary consideration.

The strategy also carries obvious risk. A Friday night main event in New York would push the fight into the early hours of Saturday morning for viewers in Britain. Organizers are effectively betting that fans will adjust their schedules rather than reject a bout many expected to unfold at Wembley.

“It’s a bloody shame, quite frankly,” Simon Jordan said on talkSPORT. “I know that MSG is a legendary arena, but not for two British fighters in a generational fight that people want to see. But I guess he who pays the piper calls the tune.”

Jordan’s criticism goes beyond nostalgia. Joshua and Fury became global stars by filling arenas and stadiums across Britain, and Wembley always felt like the natural home for the fight. Passing up the prospect of a 90,000-seat crowd in favor of a 20,000-seat arena in Manhattan signals that global streaming economics now carry more influence than staging the event where demand has been strongest for years.

If Netflix succeeds, the move may reshape how boxing’s biggest events are scheduled for the streaming era. If British television audiences fall sharply because of the timing, executives may discover that maximizing global reach can come at the expense of the audience that made the fight possible in the first place.

Sports.title: Winner Of Daniel Dubois Vs. Fabio Wardley Rematch Could Face Moses Itauma
Sports.content:
Queensberry promoter Frank Warren believes that sequence would leave the winner of the October rematch between WBO champion Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley as the logical next target. If every piece falls into place, Wembley Stadium is the preferred venue for the unification fight.

“It would be huge, absolutely huge. They’re big punchers. These guys are big, big punchers. They’re exciting. They’re not in boring fights,” Warren told BBC Sport.

The potential matchup carries another complication. Wardley and Itauma are both trained by Ben Davison, leaving the respected coach with a difficult decision if the fight comes together.

“I’ve seen best friends fight each other, but they do it for the money they get, which pays the bills,” Warren said.

First, Itauma must get past the most accomplished opponent of his professional career. Hrgovic has spent years among the heavyweight division’s leading contenders and brings considerably more top-level experience than any boxer Itauma has faced.

Winning the IBF title would leave the British heavyweight within reach of one of the country’s biggest championship fights if the remaining results go his way.

Sports.title: Jack Catterall Stuck Waiting On Romero Vs. Lopez
Sports.content:
The WBA ordered Catterall to face the winner within 180 days of his victory over Giyasov, making him the mandatory challenger for the organization’s Super championship. That ruling secured his opportunity, yet left his immediate future outside his control.

Taking a stay-busy fight carries obvious risks. A loss would erase the momentum Catterall built by winning his first world title and could jeopardize the championship opportunity now within reach. Remaining inactive isn’t an attractive alternative either, particularly in one of boxing’s deepest divisions.

Meanwhile, the 147-pound division continues to evolve. Devin Haney holds the WBO title after Keyshawn Davis declined a mandatory shot, Brian Norman Jr. continues his own championship run, and Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn remain among the division’s biggest attractions.

Staying visible is clearly a priority for Catterall. Following news that Davis would not pursue Haney, he publicly called for a fight with the WBO champion, posting, “Respect @Realdevinhaney but it’s time to get it on,” while also tagging Bill Haney with the message, “Say the words.” A day later, he followed with another brief message: “I will get my shot.”

Those posts reflect Catterall’s position. He has earned mandatory status, yet cannot negotiate the biggest fight of his career until Romero and Lopez settle the WBA picture later this month. Until then, his next move depends entirely on the outcome in Las Vegas.

Sports.title: Abel Sanchez Rejects Pitbull Cruz Fight For William Zepeda
Sports.content:
“I wouldn’t want to see that fight,” Sanchez said to Fight Hub TV.

When Villegas countered that it would produce a thrilling battle, the veteran trainer doubled down.

“I think Zepeda’s way beyond that.”

Sanchez’s comments reflected how highly he rated Zepeda’s victory over Roach. The new champion controlled the bout with constant pressure, disciplined offense and clear physical advantages to earn a unanimous decision and capture the WBC lightweight title. Last December, Cruz fought Roach to a draw, making Zepeda’s one-sided performance another point in favor of the newly crowned champion.

Sanchez explained that his objection had little to do with entertainment value. He enjoys aggressive fights, but prefers to watch skilled technicians rather than wild exchanges.

“I like action fights with technique. I don’t like action fights with just bolo punches and throwing from everywhere,” Sanchez said.

Instead, Sanchez identified WBO lightweight champion Abdullah Mason as his preferred next opponent. He also mentioned Oscar Duarte and Lindolfo Delgado as stronger stylistic matches, believing those contests would provide a better measure of Zepeda’s ability than a meeting with Cruz.

Sanchez views Zepeda’s victory over Roach as evidence that the new champion has moved into a different tier of competition, making a fight with Pitbull Cruz far less appealing than many fans believe.

Ghana News.title: NPP’s Miracles Aboagye questions Judiciary’s handling of some criminal cases
Ghana News.content:
Miracles Aboagye

Dennis Miracles Aboagye, an aspiring National Communications Officer of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), has questioned what he describes as the selective handling of criminal cases by the judiciary.

He argued that recent developments have deepened concerns about fairness in the administration of justice.

Speaking on JoyNews’ PM Express on Tuesday ahead of the NPP’s planned demonstration, Mr Aboagye said the protest was partly driven by growing unease over what he believes is the selective application of justice.

The demonstration comes amid heightened political debate over the handling of high-profile cases involving politicians and public officials. The NPP has accused state institutions of unfairly targeting some individuals while treating others differently.

When host Evans Mensah asked whether the incarceration of Ashanti Regional NPP Chairman Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, and the case involving former MASLOC Chief Executive Sedinam Tamakloe had influenced the reasons for the protest, Mr Aboagye said concerns about selective justice had become impossible to ignore.

“That is also another matter. The selective justice, the selective application of our justice system, is also obvious to all of us. It’s become even now blatant.”

Mr Aboagye revealed that he had written to the Chief Justice to express concerns about what he described as the judiciary’s closeness to the Executive.

“I wrote a letter to His Lordship,” he said.

He disclosed that although the Chief Justice did not personally respond, the Judicial Secretary issued a statement addressing some of the issues he had raised.

“The judicial secretary responded, and I thought, okay, it’s fine. At least they’ve clarified certain things.”

However, he maintained that the judiciary must remain insulated from political influence.

“I am of the view that we need to keep our judiciary very far away from our politics, far, far, far away from our politics.”

Rejecting comparisons with past administrations, Mr Aboagye insisted his concerns were based on current developments.

“I don’t take those excuses of comparisons, those excuses of what was done. I don’t care. I am a citizen. I feel that, as it is happening today, I am worried about it. I want to speak up.”

He argued that many people expected to join Wednesday’s protest shared similar concerns.

“The 10s and 1000s of people you will be seeing tomorrow on the street are simply saying that the judiciary seems to be romancing with the executive and is making the executive too comfortable.”

Pressed to explain what he meant by selective justice, Mr Aboagye pointed to the handling of criminal cases during the legal vacation.

“For example, listen, a criminal is a criminal.”

He questioned why only certain criminal cases had been selected to proceed while others remained pending.

“Now you have a lot of cases in the court, a lot of criminal cases, a lot of civil cases. Some of them predate even 2020… Every year you go on your legal vacation.

"This year, you are going on legal vacation, and you say that even though all of you are being tried for criminal cases, I have selected a few of you, and as for you, you can’t go and rest. You must go through the criminal procedure. That is selective justice.”

Ghana News.title: Judiciary is romancing the executive – Miracles Aboagye defends NPP protest
Ghana News.content:
Dennis Miracles Aboagye, an aspiring National Communications Officer of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), has defended the party’s planned protest on Thursday, August 6.

He is accusing the judiciary of becoming too close to the executive and warning that public confidence in the justice system is being eroded.

Appearing on JoyNews’ PM Express on Tuesday, Mr Aboagye said the demonstration was driven by growing concerns over what he described as the judiciary’s relationship with the government and what he called the selective application of justice.

Speaking to host Evans Mensah, he argued that the concerns extended beyond individual cases and reflected a broader perception that the judiciary was no longer keeping the necessary distance from political power.

“That is also another matter. The selective justice, the selective application of our justice system, is also obvious to all of us. It’s become even now blatant,” he said.

Mr Aboagye revealed that about a month ago he wrote to the Chief Justice to express his concerns.

“I wrote a letter to His Lordship… where I itemised my worry about his relationship and his romance with the executive, and the fact that it’s becoming too glaring.”

He said although he did not receive a direct response from the Chief Justice, the Judicial Secretary later issued a statement addressing some of the concerns he had raised.

“I thought, okay, it’s fine. At least they’ve clarified certain things,” he said.

However, he maintained that his worries had not been fully resolved.

“I am of the view that we need to keep our judiciary very far away from our politics, far, far, far away from our politics. I don’t take those excuses of comparisons, those excuses of what was done. I don’t care. I am a citizen. I feel that, as it is happening today, I am worried about it. I want to speak up.”

He said the protest was intended to send a message about the need to preserve judicial independence.

“The 10s and 1000s of people you will be seeing tomorrow on the street are simply saying that the judiciary seems to be romancing with the executive and is making the executive too comfortable.”

Explaining his concerns, Mr Aboagye said he was troubled by what he viewed as the judiciary’s visible proximity to government officials.

“I felt uncomfortable that you are looking too close. The proximity within which you seem to be moving around with these people—it’s becoming too blatant, and it makes those of us who are obviously not liked by these people uncomfortable.”

He added, “Because I get worried that these people don’t like me… if you are this way with them, and I have an issue, they probably have your ears. I don’t. How safe am I?”

On allegations of selective justice, Mr Aboagye pointed to the handling of criminal cases during the legal vacation.

“There is no way… you have a lot of cases in the court, a lot of criminal cases, a lot of civil cases. Some of them predate even 2020… This year, you are going on legal vacation.

"You say that even though all of you are being tried in criminal cases, I have selected a few of you, and as for you, you can’t go and rest. You must go through the criminal procedure. That is selective justice.”

The NPP’s planned demonstration comes amid heightened political tensions over the handling of high-profile criminal prosecutions and growing public debate over the independence of Ghana’s judiciary.

Party leaders say the protest is intended to demand fairness, equal treatment before the law and greater public confidence in the justice system.

Ghana News.title: Retired fire officer remanded over alleged GH¢303,200 recruitment scam
Ghana News.content:
An Accra Circuit Court has remanded a retired fire officer into custody over allegations that he defrauded 60 prospective recruits of GH¢303,200 in a fake Ghana National Fire Service recruitment scheme.

The court did not take the plea of Thomas Dorkenu, 60, who has been charged with defrauding by false pretences.

The case was adjourned to Aug. 12, 2026.

Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Emmanuel Nyamekye, prosecuting, told the court, presided over by Mr Kwabena Kodua Obiri-Yeboah, that Dorkenu allegedly collected the money after claiming he could secure enlistment into the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) through protocol arrangements.

The prosecution said Dorkenu allegedly informed one of the complainants, Ms Eyram Davordzi-Banini, a midwife at Akatsi, on Feb. 9, 2026, that he had secured recruitment slots from the Chief Fire Officer and asked her to mobilise prospective applicants.

According to the prosecution, Ms Davordzi-Banini mobilised 60 applicants and, on their behalf, paid GH¢303,200 to Dorkenu as what he described as approved protocol fees.

The prosecution alleged that Dorkenu subsequently issued purported appointment letters directing the applicants to report to the Ghana National Fire Service Training School on July 23, 2026.

However, when the applicants reported for training, they were informed that the appointment letters were not genuine.

The prosecution said the applicants subsequently lodged a complaint with the Chief Fire Officer, leading to investigations and Dorkenu’s arrest.

It said Dorkenu was handed over to the Police together with a Tecno Spark C30 mobile phone, believed to have been used in the commission of the alleged offence.

The prosecution said Dorkenu, in his caution statement made in the presence of an independent witness, admitted receiving the money but claimed he had also been deceived in a scam involving a Telecel telephone number.

The court heard that the mobile phone had been submitted for digital forensic examination, while Police were searching for the user of the Telecel number as investigations continued.

Ghana News.title: Board appointments of SOEs should only be based on merit – IMF to government
Ghana News.content:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has advised the government to ensure that the appointments of the boards of state-owned enterprises (SOEs) are merit-based.

It also wants audited financial statements to be submitted in a timely manner.

In its country report on Ghana, the IMF said strengthening SOE governance and oversight is essential to contain fiscal risks, as SOEs remain loss-making in aggregate, with increasing liabilities putting pressure on the central government.

“A strategic review of the SOE portfolio is necessary to reassess the rationale for state ownership and concentrate oversight on strategically important entities”, it added.

The report added that the weak tax compliance underscores the need to improve revenue administration.

Despite the introduction of digital tools, it warned that compliance gaps remain large, reflecting Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) structural weaknesses, limited the use of risk-based approaches, and operational inefficiencies, including delays in the not fully digitalized VAT refund process.

“Strengthening PFM systems is also critical to consolidate gains under the ECF, notably by expanding GIFMIS coverage to all central government entities, fully utilising the integrated GIFMIS and GHANEPS platforms, enforcing competitive procurement practices instead of reliance on single-source tenders, and achieving full visibility over government accounts to operationalize an effective TSA.

Finally, as public investment scales up, the IMF pointed out that public investment management needs to be reinforced.

The 2025 PIMA points to persistent weaknesses in project appraisal, underscoring the need to ensure that all capital projects entering the budget comply with legislated appraisal and selection procedures.

Ghana News.title: Two persons jailed for 20 years each for human trafficking
Ghana News.content:
The Tema Circuit Court “B” has sentenced two Nigerian nationals to 20 years’ imprisonment each for human trafficking and 10 years’ imprisonment for causing harm, with the sentences to run concurrently.

The court, presided over by Her Honour Mrs Naomi Adusei Amanianpong Kuntour, discharged the two accused persons, Kingsley Ndifon and Emmanuel Akong, on the first count of conspiracy to commit a crime, namely human trafficking.

Both accused persons were sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment on count two, human trafficking, and 10 years’ imprisonment on count three, causing harm.

Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Mensah Kleku, prosecuting, told the court that the accused recruited victims from various states in Nigeria and brought them to Ghana under the pretext of securing them employment.

According to the prosecution, upon their arrival in Ghana, the victims were harboured in a house at Sebrepor, a suburb of Afienya, where they were forced to engage in cyber-related criminal activities against their will.

The court heard that the accused prevented the victims from communicating with their families and compelled them to participate in illegal activities.

Victims who failed to comply with the accused persons’ instructions were allegedly subjected to severe beatings with machetes and electrical wires.

The prosecution said the victims were malnourished, in poor health and sustained cutlass wounds.

Police investigations revealed that some of the victims suffered serious injuries. They were initially treated at the Manhean Polyclinic in Tema before being referred to the Police Hospital in Accra for further treatment.

The prosecution said police later rescued the victims during an operation at Sebrepor and recovered electronic devices from the accused persons as part of investigations.

The court subsequently found the accused persons guilty of the charges of human trafficking and causing harm and sentenced them accordingly.

Ghana News.title: D. A. Twum Jnr. Fellowship officially inducts pioneer cohort
Ghana News.content:
The Daniel A. Twum Jnr. Fellowship has officially inducted its Pioneer Cohort, marking the formal commencement of a transformative journey for the next generation of Ghana's marketing communications professionals.

The induction ceremony brought together fellows, faculty members, industry leaders, and distinguished guests to celebrate the beginning of a Fellowship built on mentorship, learning, industry exposure, and leadership development. More than a ceremonial welcome, the event set the tone for an immersive experience that will equip participants with the skills, knowledge, and perspectives needed to thrive in Ghana's evolving creative industry.

Speaking at the ceremony, the Chairman of the Fellowship, Joel Nettey, encouraged the fellows to embrace every opportunity to learn, collaborate, and challenge themselves throughout the programme.

He emphasided that the Fellowship represents more than professional development—it is a platform to cultivate purpose-driven leaders who will contribute meaningfully to the future of Ghana's marketing communications industry.

Throughout the programme, the fellows will participate in masterclasses facilitated by accomplished industry practitioners, engage in agency immersions, receive mentorship from experienced professionals, and work on practical projects that bridge the gap between academic learning and industry practice.

The induction also introduced the fellows to an accomplished faculty comprising respected professionals from across the marketing communications ecosystem. Their collective expertise and commitment to mentorship underscore the Fellowship's mission of providing meaningful access to industry knowledge and preparing participants for successful careers.

Established in honour of the late Daniel A. Twum Jnr., the Fellowship continues his enduring legacy of championing talent development and creating opportunities for young creatives. By connecting emerging talent with experienced professionals, the Fellowship seeks to strengthen Ghana's creative ecosystem and inspire a new generation of innovative thinkers and industry leaders.

As the Pioneer Cohort embarks on this exciting journey, the Daniel A. Twum Jnr. Fellowship remains committed to nurturing excellence, encouraging collaboration, and empowering young creatives to transform ambition into impact.

The journey has begun, and with it comes the promise of growth, discovery, and a future shaped by creativity, purpose, and leadership.

Ghana News.title: Infantino remains Fifa president after executive meeting
Ghana News.content:
Gianni Infantino has been Fifa president since 2016.

Gianni Infantino will remain Fifa president after receiving the backing of senior executives at a meeting in Morocco on Wednesday.

Infantino summoned members of the management board to Fifa's Africa office in Rabat following mounting criticism of his aborted attempt to sell off commercial and event operations to private investors.

European football's governing body Uefa said at the weekend that it has lost confidence in Infantino, calling the Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal a "shabby, back-room, opaque deal".

Much criticism has come from within Fifa, including secretary general Mattias Grofstrom, who was at Wednesday's meeting. In an internal memo sent to Fifa staff on Tuesday, he wrote that the situation is "a sad and reproachable series of events".

However, in a statement following the meeting, Grofstrom and the management board "reaffirmed their full support" for Infantino as president.

Ghana News.title: Iran says it has agreed Strait of Hormuz shipping route with Oman
Ghana News.content:
Iran says it has reached an agreement with Oman on a shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz.

Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei did not give any further details on the agreement, which he said was "in the final stages".

Baqaei warned, however, that a deal with Oman would not, on its own, guarantee safe navigation through the strait, arguing that security remains affected by the US blockade of Iran's ports. The US and Oman have not commented on the proposal.

Since the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, Tehran has largely blocked the Strait of Hormuz through which about a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas usually passes. Since then, global oil prices have fluctuated wildly.

On Tuesday, US President Donald Trump warned that Iran would be "hit very hard" if the strait did not open "very soon".

His comments came after senior US officials said talks had progressed to allow shipments to potentially to resume later this week, though Iran has maintained that it is not negotiating with the US and has no plans to do so.

Reopening of the strait has been a key point in discussions between the two countries and mediators.

In his statement, the Iranian foreign ministry spokesman said the "geographical coordinates of the route" had been agreed with Oman.

"The factors making the Strait of Hormuz insecure still exist on the part of the United States, particularly the naval blockade and other aggressive and threatening actions against Iran and its interests," he said, according to Iran's official Irna news agency.

Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi later told Irna that the new route would be temporary and could stay open from two to four months. He did not give further details.

Since the beginning of the war, traffic through the strait has dwindled. Iran has said all passage needs to be cleared beforehand - and it has attacked vessels which have ignored the order.

One of the main points of disagreement between Tehran and Washington has been Iran's threat to impose a fee on vessels transiting the strait.

On Wednesday, Iranian officials did not say if this issue formed part of the talks with Oman.

In June, Iran and the US signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), aiming to stop fighting, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and reach an agreement to end the war within 60 days.

The deal quickly fell through, as did diplomatic talks, with tit-for-tat attacks resuming just days after the MoU was signed.

The US has maintained a naval blockade of Iranian ports in the region, while another blockade is in place on Saudi Arabia's ports in the Red Sea, imposed by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis since 20 July.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Meta’s AI model follows rivals in revealing hacks of outside systems
World.content:
Meta has said that its AI model hacked another company during cybersecurity testing, following on from recent similar announcements by rival companies Anthropic and OpenAI.

Meta said on Wednesday that one of its AI models – reported to have been Muse Spark 1.1 – made changes to the unnamed hacked company’s internal systems after accessing the public internet because of an error in the setup of the “sandbox” testing environment by independent testing company Irregular.

A “sandbox” is an isolated internal virtual testing environment, which has no access to the internet.

Last week, Anthropic said that its Claude AI model hacked into the systems of three organisations during testing that was supposed to keep it isolated from the internet.

Anthropic said a misconfiguration had allowed Claude models to reach the internet. The company said it discovered the incidents after reviewing 141,006 test sessions.

The announcement came days after rival OpenAI first revealed that its models improperly accessed the internet and went rogue during security testing.

OpenAI and Anthropic have both released their most powerful models this year, known as Sol and Mythos, respectively.

The AI Security Institute (AISI), the UK’s AI watchdog, warned in a report released on Tuesday that OpenAI’s GPT-5.6-Sol and Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 employed previously unseen levels of deception to carry out “sustained, potentially harmful activity” during a routine safety evaluation.

World.title: FAA says Trump’s Marine One briefly flew too close to passenger jet
World.content:
Air traffic controllers at Reagan National airport had failed to pause commercial flights during Marine One’s departure, sources say.

US President Donald Trump’s military helicopter Marine One briefly flew too close to a passenger jet taking off from Washington’s Reagan National airport, prompting investigations by both the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the National Transportation Safety Board.

The FAA said in a statement that its preliminary safety review of the incident on Tuesday found “a momentary loss of separation, after which the aircraft continued to move away from one another”.

The statement added that Trump was not in danger and that an air traffic controller remained in contact with both pilots throughout.

According to the Reuters news agency, two people familiar with the matter said that air traffic controllers had not paused commercial departures at Reagan National as required under the policy adopted after a crash last year.

In January 2025, a collision between a military helicopter and an American Airlines regional jet killed 67 people.

Marine One lifted off from the Ellipse near the White House at about 2:33pm local time (18:33 GMT) on Tuesday, en route to Joint Base Andrews ahead of a presidential trip to Los Angeles, according to a White House pool report.

Both the aircraft landed safely, although neither flight’s involvement has been confirmed by the FAA.

A source told Reuters that Envoy Air flight 3742, a regional jet operated on behalf of American Airlines and bound for Pensacola, Florida, was the aircraft involved, and that a second flight, Republic 4700, was separately rerouted as a precaution after coming within three miles of the airport.



The National Transportation Safety Board said it would launch its own investigation into the incident.

The near-miss on Tuesday afternoon revives scrutiny of air traffic protocols at Reagan National following the collision last year.

The crash then led to permanent restrictions on mixed helicopter and commercial traffic at the airport, along with a subsequent ban, introduced in March, on using visual-only separation for helicopters near major US airports.
